judgments.rationale: 12/12; development pass. Covers all three requested parts with distinct Rishonim explanations and useful practical differences, then separates the Mechaber and Rema regimes for external blood in salting and roasting. Named-source claims examined are supported. It carefully labels the Mechaber salting measure as synthesis and its Rishonim attributions as reports through later primary texts. No required subpart omitted; no critical failure found.

source_findings.finding: Rashba expressly attributes the several-days permission to Rabbenu Tam and explains runoff, with fish and standing-blood exceptions. His wording also permits an absorbed-then-expelled formulation; the response’s “rather than becoming retained” phrasing does not contradict that nuance.

source_findings.source: Rashi and Tosafot, Chullin 113a; Tosafot, Chullin 112b, s.v. ודגים רפו
source_findings.finding: The texts support the distinction between Rashi’s synchronized expulsion, runoff, uninterrupted absorption/expulsion, and the final no-absorption-while-expelling-juice explanation. Tosafot expressly requires the lower piece to wait under the two absorption/expulsion explanations; this is not required by the final explanation.

source_findings.source: Tur, Beit Yosef and Bach, YD 70; Shulchan Arukh/Rema 70:1
source_findings.finding: The practical differences are supported. Bach explicitly identifies removal timing. Shulchan Arukh adopts continuing juice expulsion as preventing absorption; Rema’s cavity orientation is initial practice, with permission after the fact. The nonperforated-vessel exclusion is preserved.

Rema expressly excludes separate external blood from the usual expulsion protections. Shakh requires both major loss and a mitzvah meal for the referenced post-salting heat leniency; neither response turns the end of the salting period into automatic permission.
The liquid-versus-solid and moist-versus-fully-dry limitations are real. Taz 70:2 also expressly treats the meat as hot from salting and compares incoming blood to the roast case.

The Mechaber’s limited penetration rule is a general-rule application to the stated nonfatty case, not an express Mechaber droplet ruling in 70:6. Both responses recognize that distinction. Rema’s customary sixty assessment for blood is confirmed explicitly by Shakh 76:5; no conflict should be invented from 105:9’s exceptions for other completely nonfatty prohibitions.
The Mechaber’s finger-thickness removal, cold-on-hot reasoning, separate external blood scope, and Shakh’s sixty requirement despite Rema’s silence all check out.

source_findings.source: Tosafot Chullin 113a, s.v. אין מחזיקין; Beit Yosef YD 76 quoting Rosh
source_findings.finding: The special runoff rule applies to normally expelled blood with juice and is not established for separate blood deposited externally. The cited distinction reconciles the stacked-pieces and external-droplet cases.

limitations: Independent AI development review, not a human examiner mark or practical case ruling. The pass rule is >=10/12, no zero, and no critical failure.
Only R06.md and R03.md were read for this case. Condition identity, source logs, other candidate answers, Posek instructions and repository files were not consulted.

The reviewer independently read the decisive Hebrew passages in online primary-text transcriptions. Several Wikisource pages warn of OCR or unproofread text; no printed scans or manuscript variants were collated.

The original Ran and independent writings of Rabbenu Tam or R. Yosef were not inspected; their attributions were checked in the identified transmitting texts. Rosh’s external-blood passage was checked through Beit Yosef’s quotation.

Candidate statements about having checked sources cannot be historically audited without source logs, which were deliberately excluded. The cited textual claims were corroborated; no fabricated verification was established.

No required omissions were found. Optional precision: describe Rashi’s original account separately from Tosafot’s later juice-expulsion account; distinguish general penetration rules from all quantity- and loss-dependent practical outcomes. These are not basis for a score deduction here.
